verses.text: After this Job finally spoke and cursed the day he was born.
This is what Job said:
"May the day I was born disappear, and the night that announced, 'A boy has been conceived.'
May that day go dark. May God above take no notice of it. May no light shine on it.
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it. Let a cloud settle on it, and let everything that blackens the day terrify it.
Let thick darkness take that night. Let it have no place among the days of the year and never be counted among the months.
Let that night be barren. Let no voice of joy be heard in it.
Let those who curse days curse that night, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.
Let its morning stars go dark. Let it wait for light that never comes and never see the first glimmer of dawn,
because it failed to close my mother's womb and hide this suffering from my eyes.
Why didn't I die at birth? Why didn't I breathe my last when my mother brought me into the world?
Why were there knees to receive me and breasts to nurse me?
By now I'd be lying still and quiet. I'd be asleep and at rest,
with the kings and advisers of the earth who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
or with rulers who had gold and filled their houses with silver.
Or I'd never have been here, like a stillborn child hidden away, like babies who never saw daylight.
There the wicked stop causing trouble, and there the weary find rest.
Prisoners are at ease together there. They no longer hear the voice of the one who drove them.
The least and the greatest are both there, and the slave is free from his master.
Why give light to someone in misery, or life to people whose souls are bitter,
who long for death that never comes and search for it more eagerly than for buried treasure,
who would be overjoyed and celebrate if they found the grave?
Why give light to a man who can't see where he's going, a man God has fenced in?
I sigh instead of eating, and my groans pour out like water.
What I dreaded has happened to me. The thing I feared has come upon me.
I have no peace, no quiet, no rest. All I have is trouble."
